title: Treat obesity-associated obstructive sleep apnoea with an approved medicine

concept.text: Reduce clinically significant sleep-disordered breathing pharmacologically in adults with obesity. Tirzepatide achieved an OSA indication following trials both with and without background positive-airway-pressure treatment. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity, supported by randomized trials showing clinically meaningful superiority in apnoea–hypopnoea index at 52 weeks. Test set by: FDA; the two pivotal trials enrolled 469 adults and used change in AHI as the primary efficacy measure. Reported achieved: FDA approved Zepbound for this OSA indication on 20 December 2024. Overlaps: END-05. Sources given: [FDA OSA approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-medication-obstructive-sleep-apnea) ; [Sponsor's indication-specific approval announcement](https://lilly.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fda-approves-zepboundr-tirzepatide-first-and-only-prescription).

page.title: First US approval of a medicine for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity
page.definition: A medicine has an FDA-approved indication for treating moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity. In obstructive sleep apnoea, the upper airway repeatedly narrows or closes during sleep. The apnoea–hypopnoea index (AHI) counts the resulting breathing pauses and reductions per hour of sleep. Moderate-to-severe disease begins at an AHI of 15.

goal.need: Across all body weights, an estimated 425 million adults aged 30–69 worldwide have moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea. Positive airway pressure (PAP) holds the airway open during sleep, but some people cannot tolerate the device. For adults with obesity, medication alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity can help with weight loss, reduce breathing interruptions and ease the daytime effects of poor sleep. For people already using PAP, the trials did not establish when it is safe to stop.

statements.quote: we suggest an evaluation for potential antiobesity pharmacotherapy (conditional recommendation, very low certainty in the estimated effects).
statements.context: For patients with OSA, body mass index ≥27 kg/m², insufficient weight loss despite comprehensive lifestyle treatment, and no contraindications or active cardiovascular disease.

statements.quote: Today’s approval marks the first drug treatment option for certain patients with obstructive sleep apnea
statements.context: Sally Seymour, director of FDA’s Division of Pulmonology, Allergy, and Critical Care, announcing the tirzepatide OSA indication.

statements.quote: Fast track determination was granted for OSA.
statements.context: The FDA granted Fast Track designation on 3 November 2022 for tirzepatide in the development programme for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity.

completion.title: FDA approves a medicine to treat moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity.
completion.criterion: The FDA grants the first approval of a prescribing indication for a medicine to treat moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea in adults with obesity.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, approval letter for NDA 217806/S-013 and approved prescribing information.
completion.threshold_quote: to treat moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity.
completion.basis: The approval letter establishes the indication, and the FDA identifies the approval as the first. On 20 December 2024 it approved Zepbound (tirzepatide) for this use with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

milestones.title: Phentermine/topiramate lowers AHI versus placebo at weeks 8 and 28 in a phase 2 OSA trial.
milestones.criterion: In adults aged 30–65 with body mass index 30–40 kg/m², baseline AHI of at least 15 and inability or unwillingness to use PAP as prescribed, compare phentermine 15 mg plus extended-release topiramate 92 mg daily with placebo. Both groups receive lifestyle counselling. The reduction in sleep-laboratory AHI from baseline must favour treatment at week 8 and at week 28 or early withdrawal, using the prespecified analysis adjusted for baseline body weight.
milestones.set_by: VIVUS and Kentucky Research Group, registered protocol NCT00745251, primary efficacy endpoint published in Sleep. This test is specific to phentermine/topiramate in patients not using PAP.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in AHI between baseline, Week 8, and Week 28 or early withdrawal.

milestones.title: Liraglutide lowers AHI versus placebo at 32 weeks, with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero.
milestones.criterion: In adults without diabetes who have obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA and are unable or unwilling to use continuous positive airway pressure, compare liraglutide 3.0 mg daily with placebo for 32 weeks. Both groups receive a diet prescribing a 500 kcal daily deficit and advice to exercise. For change in AHI from baseline, the two-sided 95% confidence interval for liraglutide minus placebo must lie below zero.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk, SCALE Sleep Apnea protocol NCT01557166, prespecified statistical analysis published in International Journal of Obesity. This test is specific to liraglutide in patients not using PAP.
milestones.threshold_quote: The null hypothesis was rejected on a 5% level if the two-sided 95% confidence interval (CI) of the treatment difference excluded 0.

milestones.title: Tirzepatide lowers AHI versus placebo at 52 weeks in both phase 3 OSA trials at two-sided α=0.05.
milestones.criterion: Each SURMOUNT-OSA trial tests superiority of tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg weekly versus placebo for baseline-to-week-52 polysomnographic AHI change, at two-sided α=0.05; both groups receive lifestyle intervention. The trials randomized 234 adults not using PAP and 235 using PAP. Estimated treatment differences were −20.0 (95% CI −25.8 to −14.2) and −23.8 (−29.6 to −17.9) events/h, respectively; both P<0.001. PAP users suspended therapy for 7 days before assessments. Published on 21 June 2024.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and the SURMOUNT-OSA investigators, master protocol NCT05412004, objectives and statistical analysis published in the design and results papers.
milestones.threshold_quote: demonstrate the superiority of tirzepatide at the MTD after 52 weeks of treatment, compared with placebo

milestones.title: Respiratory disturbances decline after six months of sibutramine-assisted weight loss.
milestones.criterion: In men with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA, compare the respiratory disturbance index, measured in events per hour of sleep, before and after six months of sibutramine-assisted weight loss with diet and exercise. The mean index must fall from baseline in this single-group study.
milestones.set_by: Australian National Health and Medical Research Council, primary sponsor of registered study ACTRN12605000330640.
milestones.threshold_quote: Effect on the severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea over a 6 month period.

milestones.title: Tirzepatide improves a prespecified patient-reported sleep outcome versus placebo at 52 weeks.
milestones.criterion: Show a statistically significant benefit over placebo in change from baseline to week 52 on a prespecified patient-reported sleep outcome. SURMOUNT-OSA tested the PROMIS Sleep-Related Impairment and Sleep Disturbance questionnaire scores in its multiplicity-controlled analysis pooling the two trials. The FDA also assessed each trial separately to judge whether the improvement was clinically meaningful.
milestones.set_by: FDA Division of Pulmonology, Allergy, and Critical Care, presubmission advice and multidisciplinary review for NDA 217806/S-013.
milestones.threshold_quote: meeting statistical significance on both an AHI-based primary endpoint and a PRO-based secondary endpoint would be critical to support review and registration.

milestones.title: Tirzepatide lowers AHI versus placebo at 52 weeks in adults unable or unwilling to use PAP.
milestones.criterion: In adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA who are unable or unwilling to use PAP, compare once-weekly tirzepatide at the maximum tolerated dose of 10 or 15 mg with placebo, with diet and physical activity advice in both groups. The mean reduction in AHI from baseline to week 52 on centrally read sleep studies must favour tirzepatide at a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company, SURMOUNT-OSA master protocol I8F-MC-GPIF(c), study GPI1.
milestones.threshold_quote: QW is superior to placebo for mean decrease in AHI.

milestones.title: Tirzepatide lowers off-PAP AHI versus placebo at 52 weeks in adults who use PAP.
milestones.criterion: In adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA who have used PAP for at least three months and plan to continue, compare once-weekly tirzepatide at the maximum tolerated dose of 10 or 15 mg with placebo, with diet and physical activity advice in both groups. Suspend PAP for seven days before measuring AHI. The mean reduction from baseline to week 52 must favour tirzepatide at a two-sided significance level of 0.05.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly and Company, SURMOUNT-OSA master protocol I8F-MC-GPIF(c), study GPI2.
milestones.threshold_quote: Change in AHI from baseline to Week 52 (events per hour).

not_found: Searches for FDA or society preclinical efficacy criteria for obesity-associated OSA found no numerical pass threshold.
No FDA, American Thoracic Society or American Academy of Sleep Medicine statement opposing development of a medicine for this indication was found.
